source: Clean Core Extensibility for Architects, SAP Cloud ERP Private, v20.9D, 2026-07

rules.statement: Level A is a compliance outcome, not a deployment location. It includes key-user extensibility, on-stack developer extensibility with ABAP Cloud, and side-by-side extensions using released touchpoints.
Assess whether SAP standard already satisfies the requirement before selecting an extension technology.

Prefer on-stack when the extension is tightly coupled to an S/4 process, needs strong transaction consistency, needs high-volume local data access, extends an existing core application, or mostly uses S/4 data.

Prefer side-by-side for SaaS or consumer scenarios, non-SAP users, native mobile or freestyle UX, multi-system hubs, loose coupling, independent scaling or operations, and frequent independent releases.
An ABAP Cloud consumer may remain Level A while its isolated wrapper is Level B when it wraps a classic API, or Level C when it wraps an internal SAP object. Report the composite outcome explicitly.
Place wrappers in a dedicated Standard ABAP software component or HOME package, separate from the ABAP Cloud component, and expose only a released wrapper API.
Treat a wrapper as managed debt: unit test it, monitor SAP releases for a released successor, and retire or replace it when the successor becomes available.
Use ABAP_CLOUD_READINESS to assess whether custom code can reach Level A, while recording any fallback variant as degraded evidence.

Use a governed copy of ABAP_CLOUD_DEVELOPMENT_DEFAULT for development and transport gates, including Usage of APIs, Allowed SAP Enhancement Technologies, Critical Statements, modification checks and optional security checks.
Do not create ATC exemptions for informational Level B findings. Level C exceptions require evidence that no A or B successor exists; Level D exceptions are exceptional and time-bound.
Deterministic SAP quick fixes are high-confidence. AI-generated fixes require confidence classification; lower-confidence or syntax-failing changes remain proposals for human review.
Key-user and developer extensibility may access lower layers only through released APIs and extension points. Custom fields are a preferred key-user mechanism and require lifecycle governance.

Released SAP APIs and released extension points are Level A; documented classic APIs and extension technologies are Level B; internal objects are Level C; modifications and no-API-zone technologies are Level D unless an authoritative exception applies.
Governance combines organizational responsibilities, system controls and continuous measurement. Track Clean Core Share, Technical Debt Score, Unused Code Share and Business Modifications.
Absence of classification evidence is not proof of Level D. Keep the unit ResearchRequired until release state, technology and successor evidence are established.
